title: Ezra Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezra chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezra Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezra Chapter 4.

questions.question: In Ezra 4, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard about the temple
The people of the land weakened the hands of Judah
A letter was written to Artaxerxes
questions.correctAnswer: The adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard about the temple
questions.explanation: This event occurs first in the chapter, as stated in Ezra 4:1.

questions.question: Who did the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin approach?
questions.explanation: The adversaries approached Zerubbabel and the chief of the fathers, as stated in Ezra 4:2.

questions.question: What did the adversaries claim about their relationship with God?
questions.explanation: The adversaries claimed they sought the same God as Judah and Benjamin, as mentioned in Ezra 4:2.

questions.question: What did Zerubbabel and Jeshua say to the adversaries?
options: They had nothing to do with them
questions.correctAnswer: They had nothing to do with them
questions.explanation: Zerubbabel and Jeshua told the adversaries they had nothing to do with them concerning building the house of God, as stated in Ezra 4:3.

questions.question: What did the people of the land do to the people of Judah?
questions.explanation: The people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah, as stated in Ezra 4:4.

questions.question: Who did the people of the land hire against Judah?
questions.explanation: They hired counsellors to frustrate Judah's purpose, as mentioned in Ezra 4:5.

questions.question: Until when did the hired counsellors work against Judah?
questions.explanation: The hired counsellors worked against Judah all the days of Cyrus until the reign of Darius, as stated in Ezra 4:5.

questions.question: What did the adversaries write during the reign of Ahasuerus?
questions.explanation: In the reign of Ahasuerus, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem, as mentioned in Ezra 4:6.

questions.question: Who wrote to Artaxerxes during the days of Artaxerxes?
questions.explanation: Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and their companions wrote to Artaxerxes, as stated in Ezra 4:7.

questions.question: In what language was the letter written to Artaxerxes?
questions.explanation: The letter was written in the Syrian tongue, as mentioned in Ezra 4:7.

questions.question: Who specifically wrote a letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes?
questions.explanation: Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe wrote the letter against Jerusalem, as stated in Ezra 4:8.

questions.question: The children of the captivity built the temple unto whom?
questions.explanation: The children of the captivity built the temple unto the LORD God of Israel, as stated in Ezra 4:1.

questions.question: The adversaries of Judah said they sacrificed to God since the days of Nebuchadnezzar.
questions.explanation: They claimed to have sacrificed since the days of Esarhaddon, not Nebuchadnezzar, as stated in Ezra 4:2.

questions.question: Zerubbabel accepted the offer to build the temple with the adversaries.
questions.explanation: Zerubbabel and Jeshua rejected the offer of the adversaries, as stated in Ezra 4:3.

questions.question: The hired counsellors supported the building of the temple.
questions.explanation: The hired counsellors were against the building of the temple, as stated in Ezra 4:5.

medium.title: Ezra Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezra Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who wrote a letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king?
questions.explanation: The letter against Jerusalem was written by Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe, as stated in Ezra 4:8.

questions.question: What does Ezra 4:12 promise will happen if the city is built, as described in Ezra 4:11?
options: They will pay toll and tribute
They will not pay toll, tribute, and custom
questions.correctAnswer: They will not pay toll, tribute, and custom
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:13 clearly states that if the city is built, they will not pay toll, tribute, or custom, which is a direct consequence of rebuilding the city.

questions.question: What accusation did the letter to Artaxerxes include about the Jews?
options: They are building a prosperous city
They are building a rebellious and bad city
They are seeking to honor the king
questions.correctAnswer: They are building a rebellious and bad city
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:12 describes the Jews as building a 'rebellious and bad city' which is central to the accusation made in the letter.

questions.question: What does Ezra 4:15 say about the city's historical reputation?
options: It was a city of peace
It has always been loyal to the king
It is a rebellious city that has harmed kings
It was destroyed for its worship
questions.correctAnswer: It is a rebellious city that has harmed kings
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:15 indicates that the city has a history of rebellion and has been harmful to kings and provinces.

questions.question: According to Ezra 4:14, why was it not appropriate for the companions to see the king's dishonor?
options: They were afraid of the king
They received support from the king's palace
They were enemies of the king
questions.correctAnswer: They received support from the king's palace
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:14 states that they had maintenance from the king's palace, implying a responsibility to uphold the king's honor.

questions.question: What action did the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin take when they heard about the rebuilding?
options: They sought to weaken and trouble them
They wrote to the king in favor of the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: They sought to weaken and trouble them
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:4 explains that the adversaries weakened the hands of the people of Judah and troubled them in building.

questions.question: What was the intention of the letters sent to Artaxerxes?
options: To request funds for the temple
questions.explanation: The letters were intended to inform Artaxerxes of the Jews' rebellious activities, as highlighted in Ezra 4:12.

questions.question: What does Ezra 4:10 mention about the nations involved?
options: They were brought over by Asnappar
They were enemies of the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: They were brought over by Asnappar
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:10 mentions that these nations were brought over by the noble Asnappar and settled in the cities of Samaria.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the letter sent to Artaxerxes according to Ezra 4:11?
options: To request assistance for the temple
To inform him of the rebuilding efforts
questions.correctAnswer: To inform him of the rebuilding efforts
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:11 states that the letter is a notification to the king regarding the activities of the Jews in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does Ezra 4:6 reveal about the actions taken during the reign of Ahasuerus?
options: They wrote an accusation against Judah
They were rewarded by the king
questions.correctAnswer: They wrote an accusation against Judah
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:6 indicates that an accusation was written against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem during Ahasuerus' reign.

questions.question: According to Ezra 4:5, who hired counselors against the Jews?
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:5 states that the people of the land hired counselors to frustrate the Jews' rebuilding efforts.

questions.question: The actions taken against the Jews are an example of what kind of behavior?
questions.explanation: The efforts to weaken and trouble the Jews in their building efforts represent dishonest and deceitful behavior, as shown in Ezra 4:4.

questions.question: The statement regarding the city's rebellious nature is true.
questions.explanation: The letter sent to Artaxerxes clearly states that Jerusalem is a rebellious city, as reiterated in Ezra 4:15.

questions.question: The Jews were encouraged to stop building the temple.
questions.explanation: The Jews were determined to continue building the temple as commanded by King Cyrus, as stated in Ezra 4:3.

questions.question: The letter to Artaxerxes was written in the Persian language.
questions.explanation: The writing was done in the Syrian tongue, as mentioned in Ezra 4:7.

hard.title: Ezra Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezra Chapter 4.

questions.question: What did King Artaxerxes command regarding the building of the city?
options: To cease the building until further notice
To allow the Jews to build freely
questions.correctAnswer: To cease the building until further notice
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:21 states, 'Give ye now commandment to cause these men to cease, and that this city be not builded, until another commandment shall be given from me.'

questions.question: What was found about the city of Jerusalem after the search commanded by King Artaxerxes?
options: It had made insurrection against kings
It was a newly built city
It had no history of conflict
questions.correctAnswer: It had made insurrection against kings
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:19 says, 'And it is found that this city of old time hath made insurrection against kings, and that rebellion and sedition have been made therein.'

questions.question: Who were the primary recipients of the king's letter?
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:17 mentions that the king sent an answer unto Rehum the chancellor, and to Shimshai the scribe.

questions.question: What was the consequence of the king's letter as mentioned in Ezra 4:24?
options: The work ceased on the house of God
questions.correctAnswer: The work ceased on the house of God
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:24 states, 'Then ceased the work of the house of God which is at Jerusalem.'

questions.question: What was the purpose of the letter sent by Rehum and Shimshai to King Artaxerxes?
options: To accuse the Jews of rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: To accuse the Jews of rebellion
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:12 indicates that they wrote to inform the king that the Jews were building a rebellious city.

questions.question: What did the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin want to do initially?
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:2 reveals that they approached Zerubbabel and the others, claiming they sought to build with them.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'insurrection' in Ezra 4:19 imply about the historical context of Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'insurrection' implies a strong act of revolt or uprising against ruling powers, consistent with the historical tensions in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Which literary technique is predominantly used in Ezra 4:21-22 regarding the king's command?
questions.explanation: The verses exhibit parallel structure, emphasizing the command to cease the building and the warning about potential damage to the kings.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of opposition to rebuilding efforts found in Ezra 4:4?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 4 describes opposition to the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls, echoing the challenges faced in Ezra 4.

questions.question: Which other passage in the New Testament reflects the theme of persecution for faith similar to Ezra 4:5?
questions.explanation: Acts 8:1 describes the persecution of the early church, paralleling the troubles faced by the Jews in Ezra 4.

questions.question: What comes before the king's response in Ezra 4:18?
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:18 follows the command for a search made by the king, indicating he was informed about the situation.

questions.question: What does the term 'tribute' in Ezra 4:20 signify in the context of governance?
questions.explanation: The term 'tribute' refers to the payments made by subjects to their rulers, which was crucial for maintaining the authority of kings.

questions.question: What is the historical significance of the phrase 'house of God' in Ezra 4:24?
options: It represents a physical structure only
It signifies the community of believers
It indicates God's presence among His people
It was a term used for all temples
questions.correctAnswer: It indicates God's presence among His people
questions.explanation: The 'house of God' signifies the dwelling place of God's presence among His people, emphasizing the spiritual significance of the temple.

questions.question: True or False: The work on the house of God began again immediately after the king's letter was received.
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:24 states that the work ceased and did not resume until the second year of Darius, indicating a significant delay.

questions.question: True or False: The adversaries of Judah and Benjamin were supportive of the Jews rebuilding the temple.
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:4 shows that the adversaries weakened the hands of the people of Judah, indicating their opposition to the rebuilding efforts.

theological.title: Ezra Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezra Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezra 4:3 teach about the sanctity of God's temple and the community of believers?
options: The temple is a communal project open to all regardless of faith
Only the God’s chosen people, by divine command, are to build His temple
Building the temple is optional and symbolic without divine mandate
The king’s authority supersedes the community’s role in temple construction
questions.correctAnswer: Only the God’s chosen people, by divine command, are to build His temple
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:3 states that Zerubbabel and Jeshua rejected the adversaries’ offer to help, asserting 'Ye have nothing to do with us to build an house unto our God; but we ourselves together will build unto the LORD God of Israel, as king Cyrus... hath commanded us,' affirming a divine mandate for the chosen community alone.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin and opposition to God's work is taught in Ezra 4:4?
options: Opposition to God’s work is rare and usually accidental
The people of the land weakened the hands of Judah, showing persistent human resistance to divine plans
Human opposition is always openly declared and confrontational
Opposition to God’s work comes only from external foreign powers
questions.correctAnswer: The people of the land weakened the hands of Judah, showing persistent human resistance to divine plans
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:4 explains that 'the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah, and troubled them in building,' demonstrating human opposition and sin manifesting as active hindrance to God’s redemptive work.

questions.question: What doctrine about providence and divine sovereignty is implied in Ezra 4:23?
options: God allows evil to triumph permanently without restriction
Human authorities can thwart God's work without divine permission
The cessation of the temple work was permitted by God’s sovereign will during a period of opposition
Divine sovereignty guarantees immediate success for God's people
questions.correctAnswer: The cessation of the temple work was permitted by God’s sovereign will during a period of opposition
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:23 describes that the adversaries ‘made them to cease by force and power,’ implying that God’s sovereign providence allows seasons of opposition and delay in His redemptive plans for reasons known to Him.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezra 4:19 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:19 states that a search was made and it was found that Jerusalem had a history of rebellion and sedition, demonstrating God’s attribute of omniscience as all rebellion is known and recorded.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezra 4:21 specifically demonstrate in the king's command to stop rebuilding?
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:21 commands the cessation of the building work until further orders, showing the king’s exercising of sovereign authority, which reflects God's sovereign governance over earthly events.

questions.question: How does the opposition to the rebuilding in Ezra 4 prepare for the fulfillment of God's redemptive plan in the coming Messiah?
options: It shows God's abandonment of His people until the Messiah arrives
It prefigures the rejection and opposition Jesus Christ would face as the true temple and Messiah
It suggests that rebuilding was unnecessary for salvation
It indicates that only physical restoration matters for redemption
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the rejection and opposition Jesus Christ would face as the true temple and Messiah
questions.explanation: The opposition to the temple rebuilding in Ezra 4 anticipates the rejection Jesus faced (John 2:19-21), as the temple points to Christ as the ultimate dwelling place of God’s presence.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does the accusation against Jerusalem in Ezra 4:12-16 connect to in the broader biblical narrative?
options: The theme of Israel as a rebellious city and the consequences of covenant unfaithfulness
The theme of unconditional blessing regardless of behavior
The theme of external enemies having ultimate power over God's people
The theme of the temple being irrelevant to God's covenant
questions.correctAnswer: The theme of Israel as a rebellious city and the consequences of covenant unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: The accusations in Ezra 4:12-16 describe Jerusalem as rebellious and hurtful to kings, which echoes prophetic themes warning Israel of judgment for covenant unfaithfulness (e.g., Jeremiah 22:7-9).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Ezra 4:3 and 4:23 teach about divine mandate and human opposition?
options: God’s mandate guarantees no human opposition
Divine commands are subject to human approval
God’s mandate is sovereign, but human opposition can temporarily delay His work
Human opposition can permanently thwart God’s purpose
questions.correctAnswer: God’s mandate is sovereign, but human opposition can temporarily delay His work
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:3 shows the divine mandate to build the temple, while 4:23 shows human opposition causing cessation, teaching that God’s plans are sovereign but may be temporarily hindered by human resistance.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do Ezra 4:19 and Ezra 4:21 provide regarding divine justice and human responsibility?
options: God ignores past rebellion when judging present actions
Human rebellion has no consequence on divine decisions
Divine justice takes into account historical rebellion, leading to human responsibility to stop wrong actions
God’s justice is arbitrary and unrelated to human history
questions.correctAnswer: Divine justice takes into account historical rebellion, leading to human responsibility to stop wrong actions
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:19 shows judgment based on past rebellion, and 4:21 orders cessation of rebuilding because of that, demonstrating how divine justice informs human accountability.

questions.question: What synthesis about God's providence and human political authority do Ezra 4:17 and Ezra 4:22 teach?
options: Human political authority operates independently of divine providence
God’s providence directs human rulers to act according to His purposes
Divine providence negates all human authority
God allows human rulers to act randomly without purpose
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence directs human rulers to act according to His purposes
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:17-22 shows the king’s letter commanding cessation of rebuilding, indicating God’s providence works through human authorities to accomplish His will.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the opposition in Ezra 4 shows God’s inability to protect His people from enemies. What does Ezra 4:4-5 actually teach?
options: God’s people are abandoned and left defenseless
God permits opposition to refine and test His people’s faithfulness
Enemies ultimately succeed in God’s plan
questions.correctAnswer: God permits opposition to refine and test His people’s faithfulness
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:4-5 describes continual opposition during rebuilding but does not indicate abandonment; rather, it shows God’s allowance of trials for purification and testing, consistent with biblical theology (James 1:2-4).

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of false accusation and opposition to God's work is taught in Ezra 4:8-10?
options: Opponents of God's work use truth and justice in their accusations
False accusations against God's people are a form of spiritual warfare and opposition to divine plans
Accusations always lead to immediate divine judgment
Opposition to God's work is usually honest and justified
questions.correctAnswer: False accusations against God's people are a form of spiritual warfare and opposition to divine plans
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:8-10 records letters sent against Jerusalem accusing it of rebellion to stop the temple rebuilding, showing opposition using false or politically motivated charges to hinder God's work.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by the king’s investigation and reading of the accusations in Ezra 4:18-20?
questions.explanation: The king orders a search and review of the records to verify accusations (Ezra 4:18-20), showing an attribute of impartial judgment rather than arbitrary decision-making.

questions.question: What doctrine about the continuity of God's covenant faithfulness is taught by the reference to king Cyrus in Ezra 4:3?
options: God’s covenant promises end with the exile
God uses foreign rulers like Cyrus to fulfill His covenant purposes
Cyrus acts independently of God's plans
Cyrus's command was irrelevant to the rebuilding
questions.correctAnswer: God uses foreign rulers like Cyrus to fulfill His covenant purposes
questions.explanation: Ezra 4:3 notes that the rebuilding is 'as king Cyrus... hath commanded us,' showing God’s faithfulness to His covenant by sovereignly raising a foreign king to enable restoration.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezra 4:12 and Ezra 4:13 teach about economic and political consequences tied to the obedience of God's people?
options: God's people are exempt from political and economic realities
Disobedience can lead to loss of economic privileges and political protection
Economic prosperity is guaranteed regardless of obedience
Political authorities have no interest in the obedience of God's people
questions.correctAnswer: Disobedience can lead to loss of economic privileges and political protection
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 warn that rebuilding Jerusalem would cause loss of tribute and revenue to the king, indicating the intertwining of covenant obedience with political and economic consequences.
